newsitem.title: UK: Companies say AIDS test warns of drug resistance.
newsitem.headline: Companies say AIDS test warns of drug resistance.

text.p: A new test can tell doctors whether patients with HIV are resistant to certain drugs, offering them the opportunity to avoid the waste and expense of useless treatment, two drugs companies said on Thursday.

International Murex Technologies Corporation of Canada and Belgian biotechnology company Innogenetics NV said their LiPA HIV-1 Reverse Transcriptase test was the first commercial, rapid test for drug resistance.

Current "best practice" calls for treating HIV-positive patients with a cocktail of at least three drugs, including two nucleoside-analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitors such as AZT, ddI, ddC or 3TC (lamivudine).
But many strains of the virus can quickly become resistant to one or more drugs -- especially in patients who have previously been treated with just one drug. Resistant strains can then be passed on.

"This will add another critical element for clinical decision-making and will inform both people with HIV infection and their physicians on when and what drugs to change to in the event of drug failure," Jonathan Weber, an HIV specialist at St Mary's Hospital in London, said in a statement released by the companies.
"At the moment, clinically, doctors have virtually nothing that they can use to measure resistance," Brian Gazzard of Chelsea and Westminster Hospital in London added in the statement.
"I think the LiPA test is an important step forward towards better tailoring of drug therapy to individual patient needs."
